result.topic_en: Euler applies the boundary conditions at the free end G of a vibrating elastic lamina to the total elementary force and its moment, obtaining the frequency equation 2 = cos ζ (e^ζ + e^{-ζ}) and beginning to discuss its roots.
result.transcription:
470 DE MOTV VIBRATORIO
Deinde omnium virium elementarium per arcum
F Y ſumma erat $\int p\,dx = -b^4\left(\frac{d^3 y}{dx^3}\right) =$
$-\frac{\theta^3}{b^3}\operatorname{cof.}\theta\theta t\left(A\operatorname{fin.}\frac{\theta x}{b} - B\operatorname{cof.}\frac{\theta x}{b} + Ce^{\frac{\theta x}{b}} - De^{-\frac{\theta x}{b}}\right)$
harum autem virium momentum pro puncto
Y $= \int dx \int p\,dx =$
$-\frac{\theta^2}{bb}\operatorname{cof.}\theta\theta t\left(-A\operatorname{cof.}\frac{\theta x}{b} - B\operatorname{fin.}\frac{\theta x}{b} + Ce^{\frac{\theta x}{b}} + De^{-\frac{\theta x}{b}}\right)$
quae duae quantitates a puncto Y ad alterum ter-
minum G vsque translatae vbi $x = a$, denuo euane-
ſcere debent; et ſi breuitatis gratia ponamus $\frac{\theta a}{b} = \zeta$,
has duas conditiones praebent:
$A.\operatorname{fin.}\zeta - B.\operatorname{cof.}\zeta + C.e^{\zeta} - D.e^{-\zeta} = 0;$
$-A.\operatorname{cof.}\zeta - B.\operatorname{fin.}\zeta + C.e^{\zeta} + D.e^{-\zeta} = 0$
ſupra autem iam inuenimus
$A = C + D$ et $B = C - D,$
vnde duplicem ſequentem valorem elicimus:
$\frac{C}{D} = \frac{\operatorname{cof.}\zeta + \operatorname{fin.}\zeta - e^{-\zeta}}{\operatorname{cof.}\zeta - \operatorname{fin.}\zeta - e^{\zeta}} = \frac{\operatorname{fin.}\zeta - \operatorname{cof.}\zeta + e^{-\zeta}}{\operatorname{fin.}\zeta + \operatorname{cof.}\zeta - e^{\zeta}}$
vnde elicitur
$2 = \operatorname{cof.}\zeta\,(e^{\zeta} + e^{-\zeta})$
cui ſtatim ſatisfacit $\zeta = 0$, ideoque et $\theta = 0$, quo
ipſo ſtatus quietis continetur; pro aliis valoribus
primum obſeruo, ſiue angulus $\zeta$ poſitiue ſiue negatiue
capiatur, perinde eſſe; deinde facile perſpicitur, hunc
angulum $\zeta$ recto maiorem eſſe debere, quare ne
coſinus
